title: Connection pool exhaustion on payment-service

detection.compared_against: reference window 2026-09-29T13:13:02Z → 13:43:02Z (30 min, ending 5 min before detection)

symptoms: connection_saturation rose from 0.21 to 0.97 over 14 minutes
error_rate rose from 0.4% to 3.4% on POST /authorize
18 occurrences of a previously unseen connection-acquisition failure template

conclusion.root_cause: Deployment v2.41.0 reduced DB_POOL_SIZE from 50 to 8 while refactoring the pool factory, and set DB_POOL_LEAK_GUARD=false, which disabled the guard that reclaims connections abandoned by the refactored code path. Demand exceeds the reduced capacity, and leaked connections are no longer reclaimed.
conclusion.confidence_basis: deployment diff correlates with the onset within the change window; pool config reload line confirms leak_guard=false; the failure template is new and does not appear anywhere in the 30-day baseline
ruled_out: database overload — payments-db CPU and connection counts were flat throughout
cache misconfiguration — cache-service error rate and hit ratio unchanged
traffic spike — request rate was within 4% of the weekly median

causal_claims.subject: leak_guard=false
causal_claims.detail: guard disabled in the same change that reduced pool size

ai_investigation.note: No claim of causation is asserted from temporal proximity alone. The deployment is related by preceded_by and consistent_with, and the conclusion rests on the configuration diff, not on ordering.

checks.detail: the underlying fault 'connection_leak' is still active — the remediation addressed symptoms only

verification.verdict_reason: the underlying fault 'connection_leak' is still active — the remediation addressed symptoms only; new/worsening error signatures: Cannot acquire connection from pool within <DURATION>
verification.post_settle_observation: connection_saturation resumed climbing from 0.34 to 0.89 within 6 minutes of the restart

remediation_history.rationale: Attempt 1 cleared the pool but left the fault active. The recorded failure of restart_service, plus the runbook's explicit warning that a restart will not remove a leak, point at the configuration change that disabled the leak guard.

checks.detail: the underlying fault is no longer active

verification.verdict_reason: all blocking checks passed: connection_saturation returned from 0.89 to 0.09 against a baseline of 0.21, and the underlying fault is no longer active.

lessons: restart_service clears a saturated pool but cannot remove a connection leak; it will refill within minutes
the deployment that reduced DB_POOL_SIZE also disabled DB_POOL_LEAK_GUARD, and the guard is what masks the leak in the short term
the pool config reload log line is emitted at INFO level and is easy to miss during triage
preventive_actions: add a deploy-time assertion that DB_POOL_LEAK_GUARD must be true in production
alert on pool_size changes as a configuration change, independent of the deploy outcome
promote the connection-acquisition failure template to a named alert rather than a raw log match
